title: Amazon EventBridge custom event bus (Protobuf) to AWS Lambda
description: Publishes a Protobuf-encoded event to an Amazon EventBridge custom event bus with an AWS Glue Schema Registry and delivers the decoded JSON to an AWS Lambda function

introBox.headline: How it works
text: This pattern shows how to publish a rich domain event, Protobuf-encoded, to an Amazon EventBridge custom event bus (the eventsv2 API) using PutRawEvents together with an AWS Glue Schema Registry, and then deliver that same event to an AWS Lambda subscriber.

The publisher encodes an OrderPlaced event from a .proto definition and wraps it in the AWS Glue wire format (including the message-index that tells AWS Glue which message type to decode as). Amazon EventBridge decodes the Protobuf against the AWS Glue registry server-side, before subscriber filtering, and delivers the payload as plain JSON, so the consumer AWS Lambda function needs no Protobuf library and simply logs the event to Amazon CloudWatch. A matching order_id, fields, and metadata prove the delivered event equals the one that was published.

This deploys one Amazon EventBridge custom event bus, one subscriber, an AWS Glue Schema Registry and Protobuf schema, one Java 21 AWS Lambda function with an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group, an Amazon SQS dead-letter queue, and the delivery role.
See the GitHub repo for detailed testing instructions.
